title: Reconcile a VCF Operations maintenance schedule so a retried run creates it exactly once
prompt:
Our VMware Cloud Foundation 9.0 estate reconciles its maintenance windows from a nightly pipeline, and that pipeline retries a step that looks like it failed. Right now a retry is not safe. Implement the module that makes it safe.

`module/VcfOpsMaintenanceWindow/VcfOpsMaintenanceWindow.psm1` exports `Set-VcfOpsMaintenanceSchedule`, which currently throws. It must bring one VCF Operations maintenance schedule to a requested state, driving every call through the `VMware.Sdk.Vcf.Ops` PowerCLI module. The environment installs that module; do not vendor it, and do not replace its transport with `Invoke-RestMethod`, `Invoke-WebRequest`, `HttpClient`, `WebClient`, curl or raw sockets.

`docs/contract.json` is the authority for what the module may call. It is a projection of `specifications/vcf-operations/vcf-operations-openapi.json` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at tag `9.0.0.0`, at the commit recorded in `docs/official_sources.json`. It comes from the specification itself, not from a documentation page, and not from the 9.1 revision of that same file. The only operations in scope are `acquireToken` and `getCurrentVersionOfServer` -- both performed by `Connect-VcfOpsServer`, which the caller has already done -- plus `getMaintenanceSchedules`, `createMaintenanceSchedules` and `updateMaintenanceSchedules`.

The awkward part: a maintenance schedule's `key` is unique within VCF Operations. `createMaintenanceSchedules` answers `422 - A maintenance schedule with the same key already exists`, so a run that just posts the schedule works exactly once and fails every time after. The same invocation has to be repeatable, and when it is done the schedule must exist exactly once.

The harness calls:

`Set-VcfOpsMaintenanceSchedule -Server <VcfOpsServer> -Key <string> -Hour <int> -MinuteOfTheHour <int> -DurationMinutes <int> -ScheduleType <string> [-Recurrence <int>] [-DaysOfTheWeek <string[]>] [-StartDate <string>] [-ExpirationDate <string>] [-ExpireRuns <int>] [-TimeZone <string>]`

Requirements:

- Look the key up before writing anything. Use `getMaintenanceSchedules` and filter server-side with the `name` query parameter, asking for exactly the key being reconciled. `name` is the only query parameter that belongs on that request; do not list every schedule and sift through the result locally, and do not send `id`, `resourceId`, `page` or `pageSize`.
- Match the returned schedules on their `key` exactly. A schedule that came back but does not carry that key is not the one being reconciled.
- No match: create it with `createMaintenanceSchedules`. `Outcome` is `Created`.
- One match whose schedule is already what was asked for: issue no write at all. `Outcome` is `Unchanged`. It counts as already correct only when the schedule the service holds has the same member set and the same values as the schedule this run would send; a member the caller did not supply is different from one the service is holding.
- One match whose schedule differs: correct it with `updateMaintenanceSchedules`, never with a second create. `Outcome` is `Updated`.
- More than one exact match: throw, and write nothing.
- `id` is assigned by the server. It must be absent from the create body, and it must be present on the update body carrying the id the lookup returned, because that is what makes the write land on the schedule that is already there.
- `DurationMinutes` is the schedule's `duration`. Every optional member the caller did not supply must be absent from the JSON body entirely -- never sent as `null`, `""`, `[]` or a zero-valued default. On the wire a daily window with no options is exactly `{"key":"<key>","schedule":{"scheduleType":"DAILY","duration":<n>,"hour":<h>,"minuteOfTheHour":<m>}}`.
- Return a `[pscustomobject]` whose properties are in this exact order: `Key`, `ScheduleId`, `Outcome`. `ScheduleId` is the server-assigned id of the schedule that now holds the requested state, on every outcome.

Acceptance: `pwsh -NoProfile -File verification/Invoke-Verification.ps1`. It runs the module against a loopback VCF Operations service pinned to the contract, using dummy credentials against `127.0.0.1` only, and reads that service's request log to check the exact method, target, query parameters, JSON body member set, authorization and call sequence of every request, including the omission of every unset optional member. No live VMware endpoint is contacted. Everything under `docs/` and `verification/` is protected; do not modify it. See README.md for the layout.
reference_setup: pwsh -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command "if (-not (Get-Module -ListAvailable -Name VMware.Sdk.Vcf.Ops)) { Install-Module VMware.Sdk.Vcf.Ops -Scope CurrentUser -Force -AllowClobber -Repository PSGallery }"
scenario: A retried pipeline step reconciles one VCF Operations maintenance schedule. The schedule key is unique, so a blind create succeeds once and then draws 422; the run must look the key up first and converge on create, update or no write at all.
constraint: The verifier asserts the exact request wire shape from the loopback service's request log, including that optional members the caller did not supply are omitted rather than sent as null, empty string or empty array.
environment_note: verification/contract_mock.py is a stateful loopback VCF Operations service bound to 127.0.0.1 on an ephemeral port. Its route table is built from docs/contract.json, so it serves only the operations the contract names and answers anything else 404. It enforces the specification's 422 for a duplicate maintenance-schedule key. Nothing is pre-seeded.
